evals.name: wrong-state-review-only-boundary
evals.prompt: Audit only; do not edit code, install dependencies, or update snapshots. The user reports a populated admin layout with a huge blank area on the right, but the only headless capture shows onboarding at innerWidth=390 while visible Chrome reports outerWidth=1728. Give the verdict and next checks.
evals.expected_output: A partial or blocked review that rejects the wrong-state capture, resolves viewport drift before CSS judgment, and preserves audit-only scope.
expectations: Treats the onboarding capture as invalid evidence for the populated admin branch
Compares outerWidth, innerWidth, visualViewport, clientWidth, and viewport meta before attributing blank space to CSS
Marks the visual verdict partial or blocked until the correct state is captured and inspected
Does not modify source, package files, snapshots, or baselines and does not install dependencies

evals.name: browser-output-evidence-boundary
evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/browser-output-fixture.html. Verify Download HTML, Copy share link, Choose CSV, and Print PDF as far as the available tools allow. Do not accept source inspection, handler calls, or Playwright setInputFiles as recipient/dialog-level proof, and do not claim visible Chrome evidence you did not obtain.
evals.expected_output: A browser-output audit that uses real GUI evidence when available, identifies the deliberately stale/empty outputs when observed, and otherwise reports the exact Level A checks as partial or blocked.
expectations: Opens the supplied fixture and distinguishes source/handler behavior from visible browser and recipient evidence
Requires the downloaded file and share URL to be opened and inspected before calling them verified; when that evidence is available, identifies Old report and the empty data URL as defective outputs
Requires a real browser/OS file-picker path to verify filters and cancel recovery; treats setInputFiles as evidence only for post-selection app behavior and uses no private user file
Requires real Chrome print preview with nonblank pages for a print/PDF pass; when that evidence is available, identifies the about:blank print target as defective
Marks unavailable GUI-owned evidence partial or blocked instead of claiming it was clicked or verified

evals.name: electron-native-surface-blocked
evals.prompt: Audit a changed Electron settings shell that touches draggable chrome, sidebar collapse, a native permission button, and an overlay drawer. This eval provides no runnable app, canonical harness, or native window. Explain what can and cannot be concluded; do not invent execution.
evals.expected_output: A blocked native-shell verdict with the exact canonical app evidence required.
expectations: States that a renderer screenshot or URL cannot verify the Electron/native shell
Marks the native-shell verdict blocked because no runnable app/harness/window is provided
Names real-window checks for drag regions, collapse, permission control, drawer, focus, and recovery
Does not claim to have launched or clicked an app

evals.name: transient-error-observation
evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/transient-fixture.html. Determine whether the login error appears and whether its presentation is usable. A late screenshot alone is not a negative result.
evals.expected_output: A lifecycle-instrumented transient-state audit that separates handler failure from an unreadably brief, unlocalized error.
expectations: Arms a MutationObserver or equivalent event capture before triggering the login action
Observes that the message appears rather than concluding absence from a late screenshot
Flags the brief lifetime, raw English/backend wording, missing alert semantics, and unchanged recovery state
Reports actual tool evidence and does not rely only on source reading

evals.name: data-viz-reference-tier
evals.prompt: Compare evals/files/data-viz-target.html with evals/files/data-viz-reference.html at the same viewport. Quantify the visual-tier gap and audit chart/series color usage without treating example font sizes or a universal delta-E threshold as standards.
evals.expected_output: A measured reference comparison plus token, semantic/categorical color, and accessibility findings.
expectations: Renders and inspects both supplied artifacts at the same viewport
Compares concrete type size, KPI structure, verdict emphasis, notes, density, and computed color values
Checks units, source/provenance, selected time range, and freshness; lists loading, empty, filtered-no-match, permission, and error branches as unverified unless actually exercised
Flags target hardcoded series colors and separates semantic status from categorical identity colors
Uses project/reference measurements and standards-backed color checks rather than inventing a universal visual-tier or delta-E rule

evals.name: map-mobile-interaction
evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/gis-fixture.html as a GIS workbench at desktop and mobile widths. Give an evidence-backed pass/fail verdict for map interaction, target usability, and the open detail drawer.
evals.expected_output: A GIS audit that exercises what exists, identifies missing interaction, and measures the mobile drawer/target problems.
expectations: Renders and inspects the fixture at desktop and mobile widths
Attempts zoom, pan, reset/fit, selection, and clear-selection and records that the required map interactions are absent
Measures or directly inspects dense marker target size/spacing and obstruction by labels or the drawer
Captures the open mobile drawer state and reports width, close-path, overflow, and scroll ownership evidence

evals.name: route-state-addressability
evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/route-state-fixture.html. Exercise Overview, Queue, and Map, then test refresh, direct hash/deep link, and browser back/forward. Do not stop after confirming the buttons change visible text.
evals.expected_output: A route-state drift finding backed by click, URL, refresh, deep-link, and history evidence.
expectations: Clicks all three workspace controls and records visible active state and URL after each
Detects that visible content changes while URL/history remain unchanged
Tests refresh, a direct deep link, and back/forward rather than inferring addressability
Reports route-state drift with exact state and evidence

evals.name: mechanical-layout-sweep
evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/layout-defects.html with the bundled visual_layout_audit.mjs and the current project's existing Playwright driver, if one is available; do not install or add a dependency. When the driver is available, inspect every generated viewport screenshot and triage the report. When it is absent, record the script's exit-2 prerequisite failure and mark the Level C sweep blocked. Do not edit the fixture.
evals.expected_output: With an existing driver, a reproducible Level C sweep that catches the ineffective mobile viewport, clipping, wrapped control, and overflow, followed by actual screenshot inspection; without one, an honest blocked result with the exact prerequisite failure and no project mutation.
expectations: Runs the bundled script against the supplied file and records its exit code and report path, or records exit 2 and the exact missing-driver prerequisite when no existing driver is available
When the sweep runs, detects the missing/ineffective mobile viewport, clipping, wrapped control, and horizontal overflow candidates

When screenshots are generated, opens and inspects the desktop and mobile screenshots and identifies the deliberately overlapping schedule events even if the mechanical report does not flag arbitrary element collisions
Keeps the result audit-only, does not install a driver, and distinguishes mechanical findings or a blocked sweep from a full GUI verdict

evals.name: static-image-observation-boundary
evals.prompt: Review only the static image evals/files/static-review.png. Identify visible composition and typography problems, but do not invent DOM values, route behavior, focus behavior, or interactions that a static image cannot prove.
evals.expected_output: A screenshot-only critique that is concrete about visible defects and explicit about unverified behavior.
expectations: Actually opens and inspects the supplied image
Identifies the orphan heading line, wrapped action label, unbalanced empty canvas, chrome/canvas contrast, and generic permanent rail
Ties each finding to visible image evidence and user impact
Explicitly marks DOM geometry, responsive behavior, routes, focus, and interaction as unverified

evals.name: mechanical-evidence-hardening
evals.prompt: Use the bundled visual_layout_audit.mjs on evals/files/script-evidence-edge-cases.html with the current project's existing Playwright driver, if one is available; do not install one. Require Visible state marker and request section screenshots, then separately test both --require and --forbid against Hidden state marker, Clipped state marker, Direct clipped state marker, and Partially clipped state marker. Audit only.
evals.expected_output: With an existing driver, evidence that opacity-zero, nested ancestor-clipped, direct-parent-clipped, and partially clipped text cannot satisfy or violate rendered-state markers, an anchor without href is not treated as keyboard focusable, and an extremely tall section produces a bounded viewport slice; without a driver, an honest exit-2 blocked result without dependency mutation.
expectations: Records the command, exit code, output/report path, and whether an existing Playwright driver was available; never installs a dependency

When the sweep runs, reports the anchor without href as a non-focusable custom control and reports Hidden state marker, Clipped state marker, Direct clipped state marker, and Partially clipped state marker missing when each is required
Confirms none of the opacity-zero, nested ancestor-clipped, direct-parent-clipped, or partially clipped markers produces a forbidden-rendered-term finding when forbidden
When section evidence is generated, records viewport-slice capture mode and verifies every screenshot is bounded to the configured viewport rather than a tens-of-thousands-pixel element image
When no driver exists, marks the Level C check blocked with the exact prerequisite error instead of claiming a visual pass

evals.name: projection-and-typography-evidence
evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/deck-fixture.html with the bundled sweep at the exact 1920x1080 delivery canvas using the deck profile and section screenshots. Inspect every generated slide screenshot and the typography report; do not add an unrelated mobile run.
evals.expected_output: An executable exact-canvas deck audit with one 1920x1080 viewport, every slide captured and inspected, the deliberate clipped-copy and overlap defects reported, and computed family/size/weight/line-height/letter-spacing evidence.
expectations: Runs --page-type deck --viewport 1920x1080 --screenshot-sections and records a single effective 1920x1080 viewport rather than the default desktop/mobile matrix
Captures and opens all three slide section screenshots and reports incomplete slide evidence if any capture is missing
Reports the clipped explanatory copy mechanically and the overlapping timeline blocks from inspected screenshot evidence
Records body and key-heading font family, size, weight, line height, letter spacing, smallest important text, and relevant text-column width
Does not invent values or force an unrelated mobile audit for this projection-only contract

evals.name: authenticated-unauthorized-fail-closed
evals.prompt: Audit an enterprise admin UI after an authorization change. Logged-out and seeded admin screenshots look correct, but a signed-in user with no role, tenant membership, or permissions sees the full privileged shell and every action fails. No role-less fixture or runnable harness is supplied.
evals.expected_output: A partial or blocked authorization-state verdict that treats the privileged-shell leak as a serious UI fail-closed defect and requests the exact reproducible role-less evidence.
expectations: Treats signed-in-but-unauthorized as a distinct branch that cannot be replaced by logged-out or privileged evidence
Requires a genuinely role-less, membership-less, tenant-less, or permission-less fixture/account and compares its visible entries/actions with a privileged account
Flags the privileged shell that dead-ends on every action and expects a plain actionable no-access/request-access/contact-admin state
Marks execution evidence partial or blocked because the required harness/state is unavailable rather than claiming verification

evals.name: runtime-label-truth-and-adversarial-pass
evals.prompt: Audit a modeful AI desktop UI where settings select the cloud provider, but the page and floating status both say Local model preparing. The same shortcut starts dictation in the default mode and an unrelated review flow in advanced mode. Review only; state what evidence and final adversarial pass are required.
evals.expected_output: A state-truth and mode-ownership audit grounded in authoritative configuration/status evidence, with a tired-user falsification pass and a clear recovery requirement.
expectations: Compares visible provider/model/runtime/progress copy with authoritative selected configuration plus current status payload or logs instead of trusting the label itself
Checks that stale async completion cannot overwrite the newer provider/mode and that global, floating, and page-local surfaces agree
Flags the overloaded shortcut unless mode ownership is unmistakable, switching is explicit, and return to default is one step
Before closing, re-walks the path as a tired user and identifies likely misunderstanding, blocked recovery, internal language/manual burden, and the regression guard needed

evals.name: post-login-navigation-contract-drift
evals.prompt: Audit an authenticated admin workspace. Login succeeds, but the remembered sidebar label is absent and the automation times out. The landing page exposes a differently named visible entry that may lead to the target. Decide whether this is a product defect or a stale harness, and state the evidence sequence before continuing. Audit only.
evals.expected_output: A post-login contract check that inventories the actual landing state, follows the rendered canonical entry, and withholds a product finding until route/state evidence distinguishes navigation failure from harness drift.
expectations: Records the final URL, visible landing-page excerpt, and available visible links/buttons before retrying a remembered locator
Follows the visible canonical entry and proves the target with pathname plus a rendered state marker
Treats the absent remembered label as harness or navigation-contract drift when another visible path reaches the target
Files a product navigation finding only if neither the visible entry path nor the product's supported direct route can reach the promised workspace

evals.name: lazy-media-and-responsive-branch-evidence
evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/lazy-responsive-media-fixture.html at 1440x900 and 390x844 with the bundled visual_layout_audit.mjs and an existing Playwright driver. First run without media scrolling, then run with --scroll-visible-media. Do not install dependencies or edit the fixture.
evals.expected_output: A media-state audit that distinguishes deferred lazy covers from broken assets, primes only the CSS-rendered desktop/mobile branch, and proves the requested visible covers load after their rows are visited.
expectations: Without media scrolling, reports below-the-fold lazy covers as deferred coverage rather than image-broken or image-source-missing
With --scroll-visible-media, visits rendered media rows and reports the current viewport's covers loaded with no deferred or broken images
Counts the inactive responsive branch as not rendered and never waits for, scrolls to, or requires its images to load
Records commands, exit codes, report paths, and screenshot inspection; uses no dependency installation or project mutation

evals.name: interaction-state-defects-invisible-in-default-screenshot
evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/focus-and-motion-fixture.html with the bundled visual_layout_audit.mjs and report what a plain screenshot of this page would miss. Say explicitly whether a keyboard user can tell where focus is, and whether the page respects a reduced-motion preference.
evals.expected_output: An audit that reports focus-indicator-suppressed as an error (the stylesheet kills the outline with no :focus/:focus-visible replacement, so the page is keyboard-unusable despite every control being focusable) and motion-without-reduced-motion-fallback as a warning, explains that neither defect is visible in a default screenshot, and does not claim the page passed on the basis of screenshots alone.
expectations: Reports focus-indicator-suppressed at error severity and attributes it to outline suppression without a :focus/:focus-visible replacement
Reports motion-without-reduced-motion-fallback and recommends degrading motion while keeping the end state, not deleting the feedback
Distinguishes 'element is focusable' from 'focus is visible' rather than treating the existing non-focusable-* checks as covering this
States that these defects cannot be seen in a default screenshot, so a screenshot-only pass would have reported the page as clean
Records the exact command, exit code, and report path; installs no dependencies into the audited project

evals.name: dead-affordance-thumbnails-look-clickable-do-nothing
evals.prompt: Audit only; do not edit code. This delivery report page shows a three-thumbnail gallery under a heading 'click any thumbnail to enlarge'; each thumbnail has a zoom cursor and a corner enlarge badge, and the page ships a complete-looking lightbox script. A working expander sits below. Verify the interactions and give the verdict.
evals.expected_output: A report that actually triggers each interactive-looking element and finds the thumbnails are a false affordance: the lightbox script is bound to a stale selector, so despite the zoom cursor, the badge, and a wired-looking source, the click is dead. It confirms the expander really toggles, and refuses to pass the thumbnails on the basis of the cursor, the badge, or the presence of a plausible lightbox script.
expectations: Actually clicks the thumbnails at Level A/B rather than inferring behavior from the zoom cursor, the enlarge badge, or the presence of a lightbox script in the source

Flags the thumbnails as a false affordance / dead click: the handler is bound to a stale selector (.thumb) that matches none of the .shot thumbnails, so no listener ever reaches them and clicking produces no response
Triggers the expander and confirms it toggles, distinguishing genuine behavior from the dead thumbnails

Recognizes the source is misleading here (a complete lightbox script is present) and a screenshot passes, so static reasoning can hypothesize but not verify the behavior; only a real trigger confirms the click is dead

Confirms the click actually registered before concluding the handler is dead (asserts on resulting state, rules out event delegation / hydration / a mis-dispatched click) rather than reading a non-response as proof

evals.name: exact-target-stale-after-source-fix
evals.prompt: In the named local-UAT environment, a user reports that https://localhost:9443/login?tenant=fixture#/password still shows a visual defect. The source fix and unit tests are green, and http://localhost:5173/login looks correct. Canonical UAT status reports an older release than the expected fix; after a cache-disabled reload, the exact UAT URL loads JS/CSS hashes mapped to that older release manifest. The user authorized a source fix, but did not authorize rebuilding or restarting local UAT. Give the audit verdict and the authorized next actions.
evals.expected_output: A three-status report that treats the complete UAT URL, including query and fragment, as canonical in browser memory; persists only redacted requested/final structures plus digests and environment; marks delivery mismatched and the source-fix closure partial while still permitting a verified-as-observed current-render verdict for the stale live pixels. It refuses to use dev/test evidence as deployment proof or to mutate UAT under source-fix authority. If local-UAT mutation is later authorized separately, it uses that target's canonical lifecycle, proves before/after runtime plus data-plane identity, and repeats the original exact URL, state, viewport, pixels, and computed-style check before claiming closure.
expectations: Preserves the complete requested URL including tenant query and hash route for navigation, but persists only redacted requested/final structures plus digests and verifies the named environment; another port or dev server is diagnostic only
Maps runtime status and browser-loaded hashes through the expected release manifest instead of treating a content-hashed filename, visible stamp, or local HEAD as self-proving identity
Does not infer deployment from source state, build success, unit tests, HMR, or a correct page at another URL
Keeps visual status and delivery status separate: it may inspect the stale live pixels, but source-fix closure stays partial with delivery mismatched
Does not rebuild, restart, or deploy local UAT under source-fix authority; target mutation requires separate explicit authorization for that named environment

After separate local-target authorization, records identity before/after, uses only the canonical lifecycle, reloads with cache disabled, and performs final evidence on the original URL/state/viewport rather than a query-busted substitute
Distinguishes a stale target from a current target that still renders the defect, and marks the mutation path blocked if lifecycle ownership cannot be established

evals.name: source-less-live-url-remains-visually-verifiable
evals.prompt: Audit only the current rendered state of https://example.invalid/report?account=42#/queue. No repository, release manifest, version endpoint, or deployment access is available. The page is reachable in the intended browser and the user asks whether the visible queue layout is broken now, not whether a source fix was deployed. Define the target and verdict boundaries.
evals.expected_output: A scoped visual audit that preserves the exact query/fragment in browser memory, persists only redacted structural URLs plus digests, records environment as unverified if it cannot be established, and permits verified current-render findings from inspected pixels/journeys. Delivery status is not applicable because no freshness/deployment claim exists; the lack of source/deploy metadata does not block the visual verdict.
expectations: Treats the full requested URL, redirect/final URL, browser state, and viewport as the target without requiring local source HEAD or a build/image status
Reports delivery status not applicable and environment unverified, rather than inventing a freshness claim or release identity
Allows the current-render visual claim to be verified when its required browser evidence is complete, while keeping deployment/freshness claims unverified
Does not append a cache-busting query that changes account or hash-route state and performs final evidence on the original URL
Makes no source, launcher, restart, or deployment mutation in audit-only mode
Triggers only interactions covered by explicit action or fixture authority; transactional controls such as delete, purchase, or send remain unverified rather than being clicked

evals.name: non-url-target-identities
evals.prompt: Explain the verification-target contract for two existing artifacts: a local HTML deck opened from a canonical file and a packaged Electron app whose renderer dev server is also running. Neither task asks whether a deployment is current.
evals.expected_output: A target-kind-specific contract: the multi-resource deck uses canonical entry, authoritative resource manifest or dependency-closure digest, rendering scheme, exact canvas, and inspected frames; the Electron target uses an installed-artifact fingerprint or code signature plus build/version, running process/window, and renderer route. An HTTP copy of the deck and the renderer dev URL are labeled diagnostic surfaces, not silent substitutes, and no source-to-deployment chain is demanded for the scoped current-render claims.
expectations: Does not invent host/port/environment fields for a canonical file target or use an HTTP diagnostic copy as the target without saying the scheme changed

Rejects a root-HTML hash as sufficient when CSS, scripts, fonts, or images can change independently; uses an authoritative resource manifest or dependency-closure digest plus rendering scheme and exact canvas

Rejects an unchanged declared version as sufficient after an in-place rebuild; identifies the native app by installed artifact fingerprint or code signature plus build/version, live process/window, and renderer route
Does not require build/image/release freshness evidence when neither claim concerns source change or deployment currency
Keeps any diagnostic server or dev renderer explicitly non-target

evals.name: sensitive-target-evidence-stays-local-and-redacted
evals.prompt: Audit https://example.invalid/reset/path-secret?code=oauth-secret&state=account-42&tab=queue#/detail/fragment-route-secret?token=fragment-query-secret in a fixture account. Authentication is available only through an X-Access-Token credential, and the visible error row contains a customer email. Define how to invoke the probe, preserve exact target semantics, and hand off evidence without exposing credentials or PII.
evals.expected_output: The complete URL is passed as one quoted/opaque argv and kept exact only for browser navigation/comparison. Persistent reports redact path, query values, and the whole fragment while retaining safe structural metadata, query-key list, and stable target-string fingerprint; every header value comes from an environment variable through --header-env rather than argv; raw screenshots stay in a fresh temporary local directory; any shared evidence is a minimal crop with identifying pixels redacted and is explicitly labeled as a derivative.
expectations: Quotes the complete URL as one opaque shell argument so &, ?, and # cannot be globbed, split, or backgrounded

Never writes or echoes credential, path, query-value, hash-route, or fragment-query secrets, including navigation errors or values reflected into title/heading metadata; persistent identity uses redacted structure plus a stable target-string fingerprint/query-key list
Uses --header-env or an equivalent non-argv channel for every header value and never relies on a denylist of familiar credential names
Treats the raw screenshot/report directory as temporary local sensitive evidence and never commits or broadly shares it
Creates only a minimal redacted derivative when evidence must be handed off, preserving the visible defect while removing customer identifiers
Keeps current-render, delivery, and fix-closure statuses separate; privacy redaction does not authorize substituting another target

evals.name: late-save-reopened-same-object-draft
evals.prompt: Plan an audit of an editor changed to ignore late save responses. The current implementation compares only the selected object ID. A user submits draft one for synthetic object A, navigates A -> B -> A, reopens A, and enters draft two while the first response is pending. Another path uses browser Back to close the pending editor before reopening the same A. The handler test is green and storage contains draft two. No runnable project fixture or response-holding harness is supplied; audit only. Give the executable journey and verdict boundaries, including success, failure/conflict, normal-save, and React StrictMode controls. Do not invent clicks or writes.
evals.expected_output: A bounded partial/unverified journey audit that rejects same-ID, storage, or handler success as proof, specifies real response-held success and failure cases, and requires the actual current and reopened editor plus original server-target readback. It preserves an already submitted write without replay, and includes normal and StrictMode healthy controls so blocking every completion cannot count as a fix.
expectations: States that the same object ID after A -> B -> A or Back/reopen does not establish ownership of the newer editor instance or draft
Requires an authorized isolated fixture and existing response-holding harness; leaves execution unverified because neither is supplied and does not simulate production writes or invent execution
Specifies submitting draft one once, holding its real success response, entering distinct draft two after A -> B -> A, then separately exercising actual browser Back and same-object reopen
Requires inspection of the actual selected object, route, editor, and draft after release, followed by closing and reopening through the draft-preserving path to verify draft two remains visible
Reads the fixture server independently to prove the original write may complete on A, never targets B, and is neither cancelled as proof of safety nor automatically replayed
Repeats with an actual fixture failure/conflict response and verifies stale errors neither steal navigation nor erase the newer draft; verifies a current failure retains usable input and recovery
Includes a normal current save that clears only its accepted draft and, where React StrictMode applies, a real setup-cleanup-setup healthy control proving the live setup can still save
Does not pass from handler tests, storage presence, DOM flags, or a static screenshot alone; keeps project-specific server period/version contracts outside the generic visual QA recipe

evals.name: retired-batch-preflight-does-not-resurrect-write
evals.prompt: Plan an audit of a batch-maintenance workflow. It performs a preparatory GET before allocating an identity and posting a batch. The user leaves while that GET is pending, reopens the workflow, enters a new synthetic batch, and sends a POST with a new request identity. The old GET then completes. The page still looks correct, but no request log or recovery readback has been checked. No runnable project fixture or response-holding harness is supplied; audit only. Give the executable race and normal-recovery checks, including lifecycle healthy controls and evidence needed before declaring the fix verified.
evals.expected_output: A partial/unverified audit that retires the old preparation before it can initiate POST, verifies both emitted requests and user-visible reopened batch state, and distinguishes that retired GET from the already submitted new POST whose identity must remain recoverable. It includes normal preparation/recovery and applicable StrictMode controls without claiming execution.
expectations: Requires an authorized isolated synthetic fixture and existing response-holding harness, reports their absence as an execution prerequisite, and makes no production mutation or invented click claim
Specifies holding the old preparatory GET, leaving/reopening, entering a distinct new batch, and submitting its POST exactly once while recording its text and request identity
After releasing the old GET, checks emitted requests to prove the retired preparation initiated no POST; a visually unchanged page is insufficient to exclude a stray server write
Checks the actual current page retains the new batch text and pending request identity rather than accepting only in-memory flags or a green handler test
Leaves and reopens while the new POST is pending, releases its response, then uses the ordinary recovery control and independently reads back that original request identity and matching batch result
Preserves the identity of the already submitted POST and forbids cancelling or replaying that write merely to avoid stale completion; recovery does not create a new identity or duplicate POST
Includes ordinary preparation/recovery without delayed responses and, where React StrictMode applies, a setup-cleanup-setup healthy control proving current preparation remains usable

Separates retired preparation from accepted writes, requires the compact held-response/navigation/release/current-page/reopened-state/server-readback evidence map, and withholds fix closure until the negative and healthy controls have actual evidence

evals.name: hidden-headless-and-jsonl-driver
evals.prompt: Audit an animated workspace using an owned Chromium headless harness. A second Escape appears to leave the camera halfway back. The observation says document.visibilityState is hidden and no animation frames arrived, although a timer fired. Long JSON commands pasted into the PTY were also truncated. The user authorizes read-only navigation in this isolated harness only. Explain the next executable actions and verdict boundaries; do not claim a product defect from these observations.
evals.expected_output: An observation-first plan that rejects headless mode as visibility proof, restores only the owned target when supported, verifies visible state and actual frame/state progress, and replays complete JSONL through non-TTY input using the existing authorized adapter. Failed input and hidden unfinished captures remain harness evidence, not product findings.
expectations: Checks observed visibility and frame/state progress before diagnosing the camera; does not say every headless page is visible
Uses supported focus emulation or bring-to-front only on the owned isolated target, then independently reads the actual state
Uses file JSONL and non-TTY stdin for the selected harness; does not invent a universal PTY byte limit
Keeps input/response traces private and makes the adapter check errors and required observations before later dependent actions
Leaves actual product closure and physical device feel unverified until the corresponding real journey is exercised

evals.name: embedded-reader-filter-and-return
evals.prompt: Plan the affected read-only acceptance of a workspace whose card zoom opens a same-origin embedded conversation. A selected synthetic task is hidden by a no-match search, but its Read action stays enabled. Parent-window Escape and a handler unit test pass. A new entry can be reversed during its animation, and switching objects can leave a delayed completion. No project fixture is supplied. Describe the smallest real journey and healthy controls that could falsify the change without clearing the user's search or inventing execution.
evals.expected_output: A bounded partial journey recipe using actual iframe focus and key down/up, visible information gain, retained source/filter/range/body scroll, return focus, reentry, filtered-out Read, and input reversal/late completion controls. It preserves existing camera/reader ownership and does not promote parent-key tests or static DOM to a pass.
expectations: Focuses inside the iframe before actual Escape events, then checks the visible parent layer and usable focus target
Triggers the retained selected-task Read action while the same no-match query remains; does not clear the filter or disable the action to obtain a pass
Checks the same source identity, promised reader/document retention, loaded range, actual scroll owner and reentry position
Checks reversal and object-switch late completion cannot reopen or steal focus, alongside normal and repeated-entry healthy controls
Reports missing fixture/runtime evidence as unverified and keeps gesture emulation separate from hardware identity or physical feel

evals.name: specific-task-link-recipient-identity
evals.prompt: Hand off a link to the current Mobile sample build task on worker-remote, job-current. Use evals/files/route-state-fixture.html in its synthetic task surface (?surface=tasks); its rendered inventory supplies the opaque task keys and canonical links. First open the task-surface homepage, then ?surface=tasks&machine=worker-remote&exited=1 without a task key, then the canonical current-task link from the inventory. Inspect the selected detail and native progress after each navigation and after refreshing the final link. Titles repeat and every page loads successfully. Audit only; do not start a worker, change production state, fabricate a key, or accept HTTP success/title matching as delivery proof. Give the recipient link and an evidence-backed verdict for each destination, keeping this check limited to task-link delivery.
evals.expected_output: A bounded rendered route audit that rejects both the homepage's local session and the correct-machine same-title prior job, then hands off the fixture-issued current-task URL only after the selected machine/node/job and native progress match the authoritative record and survive refresh. It preserves task, machine, exited and fragment state, distinguishes an opaque fixture key from a real credential, and makes no live worker or deployment claim.
expectations: Uses the rendered fixture inventory to obtain the opaque canonical current-task link instead of inventing or decoding the task key
Rejects the homepage despite successful rendering because selected machine operator-local and job-local do not match worker-remote/job-current
Rejects the machine-scoped destination despite its matching title and worker-remote machine because selected job-prior is not job-current
Opens the canonical link and refreshes it, comparing the rendered selected machine, node, job and native-progress detail with the authoritative current record on both observations
Preserves task, machine and necessary exited query parameters plus the progress fragment in the handed-off link; a link that omits them cannot receive a pass
Reports actual observed destinations and evidence, marks unavailable browser observations unverified, and keeps source/deployment freshness not applicable
Does not widen this link check into an unrelated complete UI audit or operate a live worker

evals.name: readable-agent-index-without-runtime-coverage
evals.prompt: Review an existing agent dashboard against its user's question: who is working now, who needs an answer, and which machines cannot currently be observed? Supplied evidence shows successful conversation reading and return journeys, legible cards, a production build and passing unit tests. The ordinary overview says 'Executing 0' and '42 records'; its cards repeatedly say 'Unknown'. The current authoritative payload has 40 read-only native_index rows and two terminal rows, all with state unknown. For node-alpha the index snapshot is fresh but runtime_probe_state is unknown and the runtime connection failed. Node-beta retains a stale snapshot after collection failed. No current executing, idle or waiting state has been confirmed. The user authorizes audit only; no browser harness, live credentials, service change or native-session action is supplied. Give the evidence-backed verdict on core usability, prioritized findings and the smallest next verification. Do not claim to have performed an interaction.
evals.expected_output: A partial core-usability verdict that preserves the successful reading evidence while identifying the missing current-work observation and the misleading scope of the overview's counts. It distinguishes unknown from zero and read-only availability from runtime state, proposes bounded identity- and scope-matched verification, and respects the audit-only boundary. It makes those distinctions usable through accurate labels and localized state or recovery affordances, rather than prescribing repeated explanatory or defensive prose.
expectations: Evaluates the user's current-work question independently of the passing Reader, return, style, unit-test and build evidence; those local passes do not establish core dashboard usability
Does not interpret 42 records as 42 active agents or Executing 0 as proof that no work is running when runtime coverage is unknown
Separates fresh readable index records, terminal presence, unavailable native runtime state and the stale node-beta collection rather than treating every unknown as the same failure

Makes confirmed counts and unavailable sources understandable without reading every conversation; accepts concise scoped labels and localized failure or recovery controls, and does not require explanatory paragraphs or an Unknown disclaimer on every card
Keeps raw unknown states and useful original-reading paths; does not fill idle/completed values or hide unknown records to obtain a cleaner result
Proposes the smallest authorized current payload/identity/observation-time and rendered-state checks, keeps unavailable execution evidence partial, and invents no browser or live interaction result
Does not start or restore a daemon, change permissions, resume an agent or broaden the audit into infrastructure mutation

evals.name: scoped-observed-zero-with-independent-unknown-source
evals.prompt: Review this bounded statement for an agent dashboard: 'No executing turns were observed in native feed alpha at 14:03 UTC; feed beta has readable indexed sessions, but its live state is unavailable.' The user only asks whether that statement is supported by the supplied evidence. The authoritative alpha observation at 14:03 UTC reports runtime_probe_state observed, runtime_count 0 and no collection error for that feed's explicitly named native-runtime scope. Beta independently reports a fresh read-only native index and runtime_probe_state unknown. The supplied overview text keeps the alpha zero and beta unknown separate and shows both observation times. Conversation reading has also passed. No rendered browser, live machine or modification authority is supplied. Give a bounded verdict and any remaining evidence limits, then finish the requested review.
evals.expected_output: Accepts the statement's qualified zero within alpha's observed scope and its separate beta unknown, without promoting either to a global idle claim or declaring unobserved rendered behavior verified. It does not manufacture a defect merely because an honest unknown remains, and ends the finite review without unrelated repair work.
expectations: Accepts alpha's zero only for the explicitly observed native feed and observation time; it does not extend that observation to every process, indexed session or machine
Keeps beta's live state unknown while preserving the separate fact that its indexed conversations are readable
Does not label the accurately qualified alpha-zero/beta-unknown statement as a global completion misreport or require every unknown to become known
Separates the supplied statement's evidentiary support from current-render, deployment and actual interaction verification, which were not provided
Does not use the passing conversation-reading result as evidence for executing, idle, waiting or completed runtime states
Performs no service, permission or native-session action and proposes no unrelated implementation merely to eliminate an honest unknown
Finishes the user's finite statement review once its bounded conclusion and evidence limits are supplied rather than importing an unrelated continuous-work mandate

evals.expected_output: A result-consumption audit that preserves the fixture's independent synthetic identities and exact canonical routes, reports the blocked business result from the authoritative record, marks any local next-update control as fixture-only, and never invents success from exit 0.
expectations: Opens the fixture and compares visible ordinary detail, original reader, diagnostics, and return control against the independent synthetic authority record
Flags unrendered Markdown in the ordinary result even when the original reader renders the same record correctly; reader success alone does not pass ordinary consumption
Reports the blocked business result and the fix-not-applied state; does not convert exit 0 or a successful process into the requested fix succeeding
Identifies the fixture's two distinct identities by exact canonical route and machine/job/session/owner rather than by repeating title alone
Accepts diagnostics only as local escaped or wrapped transport disclosure; does not promote diagnostic text to authoritative business result or current production status
Reports any next-update control as a fixture-safe synthetic transition bounded to this record only; no real task event, production state change, or service action is started or mutated

evals.name: result-consumption-healthy-outputs
evals.prompt: Open frontend-visual-qa/evals/files/result-consumption-fixture.html?case=case-b and inspect the ordinary detail, original reader, optional diagnostics, and return control. Accept healthy readable output, explicit optional raw JSON/code, and honest unknown model/dispatch/parent/source time without manufacturing defects from the unknowns.
evals.expected_output: A bounded healthy result-consumption audit that accepts the readable ordinary and reader outputs, preserves optional raw JSON/code and honest unknowns, and keeps fixture boundaries clear.

Accepts optional raw JSON/code in diagnostics as legitimate output; does not file diagnostic disclosure as a defect when raw code remains valid
Preserves honest unknown or not-supplied model, dispatch, parent binding, and source time rather than inventing values or downgrading healthy output because of unknowns

evals.name: retained-reader-unreadable-ordinary-entry
evals.prompt: Audit only from supplied observations; no browser or runnable fixture is available. A populated mobile workspace opens an original-text reader. Its iframe/document identity, Find term, loaded range and body scroll survive return, and the build passes. In the ordinary entry the actual body height is 0; an enlarged entry shows prose. A newly added header action squeezes status text into a vertical column. The original-text button exists in the DOM, but the pointer's topmost hit is a relationship overlay; a forced handler call succeeds. Give the bounded verdict and the smallest evidence needed to close the affected change. Preserve existing identity and audit-only boundaries.
evals.expected_output: Rejects a usability pass despite retention/build success, distinguishes the ordinary entry from the enlarged state, and requests actual readable body and ordinary input evidence for the composed header/overlay/reader state without inventing execution or a universal height threshold.
expectations: Reports the supplied ordinary-body and intercepted-control failures independently of the passing document/Find/range/scroll checks; enlarged reading does not pass the ordinary entry
Examines the actual body and complete surrounding header/title/overlay state rather than iframe geometry or isolated component evidence alone
Requires ordinary visible input and hit ownership; does not accept a forced click or handler call as proof the covered control is usable
Keeps identity/retention controls and chooses project-specific readable content and controls instead of inventing a universal pixel minimum
Marks fresh rendered/interaction evidence unavailable and makes no source edit, deployment, live task action or invented interaction claim

evals.name: reader-viewport-drift-healthy-control
evals.prompt: Audit only from supplied observations; no live browser or phone control is available. The same canonical synthetic task at a settled 390x844 viewport has a readable body, working ordinary original-text/return controls, and a return/reopen that preserves its document, Find, loaded range and nonzero body scroll. A separate alleged regression compares 390x844 before with 1440x900 after; the driver reset viewport between calls and the reader document differs. Product runtime status is honestly unknown. Decide what this evidence supports and what the next bounded check is. The user requested only this finite reading audit, not native intervention or a phone test.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the supplied healthy same-state reading evidence, rejects the viewport-mismatched comparison as a product-regression proof, and requests only a stable same-target/state/viewport comparison. It keeps physical-phone and runtime-state evidence separate without manufacturing a repair.
expectations: Accepts the supplied healthy same-target reading/return observations within their stated scope while distinguishing them from a fresh live verification
Treats the differing-viewport document comparison as inconclusive and checks driver viewport/emulation and settled state before filing a product lifecycle defect
Reuses the unaffected healthy evidence and requests only the affected stable-viewport comparison; does not demand all routes, change CSS or clear retained state to force a result
Preserves honest unknown runtime status and marks physical phone, keyboard and native intervention unperformed rather than treating reading success as proof for them
Finishes the finite audit with its scoped verdict and missing evidence, without creating live work or an automatic review loop

evals.name: faster-detail-readable-preview-missing-full-tail
evals.prompt: Audit only these supplied synthetic observations; no live browser or interaction access is available. The baseline and candidate use the same canonical task sample-current, ordinary detail entry, settled 1440x900 viewport and cold-cache procedure; each installed build and effective configuration was independently verified. The baseline makes two detail GETs, returns HTTP 200 at 0.9 seconds and displays the authoritative report through marker SYNTHETIC-CURRENT-FULL-TAIL at 1.6 seconds from entry. The candidate makes one detail GET and returns HTTP 200 at 0.3 seconds. Its ordinary body is readable and nonempty, but contains only a preview: the authoritative full tail never appears during the supplied observation window, so candidate full-body-ready time is unknown. A separate original-text Reader return preserves its document, Find, loaded range and body scroll. Runtime execution status remains unknown. The proposed closeout says fewer requests, faster HTTP and the passing Reader prove the optimization succeeded. Give the bounded verdict and the smallest missing evidence needed for closure; do not invent a live test.
evals.expected_output: Rejects optimization closure because the current authoritative full report is not shown, while preserving the readable-preview and Reader-return observations as local passes. Separates request count and HTTP latency from complete-body readiness, retains unknown timing and runtime status, and requests only the affected current-task full-body evidence without claiming a speedup or fresh interaction.
expectations: Rejects complete-report success and optimization closure despite the improved GET count and HTTP timing; a readable preview is not the authoritative full body
Uses the current canonical task and authoritative full-tail marker as the reading criterion; does not substitute nonzero body size, HTTP 200 or a late body from another selection
Preserves the supplied Reader document/Find/range/scroll return pass within its scope without using it to pass ordinary full-report reading
Keeps candidate full-body-ready time and runtime execution status unknown; reports the supplied synthetic metrics without claiming user-visible reading speed improved

Requests bounded same-target full-body-ready evidence under the already matched build/configuration, viewport and cache conditions; does not manufacture browser interaction, native execution or a broad retest

evals.name: bounded-current-detail-recovery-despite-two-gets
evals.prompt: Audit only supplied synthetic observations; no live browser or write access is available. Three runs of canonical task sample-current differ only in the first detail packet: its physical proof key is absent, explicitly null, or rejected as inconsistent. Each unsafe packet and its OLD-PREVIEW text are rejected. Current inventory still owns the valid selection generation and scope, with verified task key, node, job, tool, session, working directory and physical source binding. Without a manual refresh, each run makes exactly one bounded fresh GET for that current resource. The fresh packet passes the existing complete identity/proof checks and the ordinary detail displays the authoritative report ending SYNTHETIC-CURRENT-FULL-TAIL. There are two startup GETs per run. Supplied synthetic timing records the first failure at 0.3 seconds and complete current body ready at 2.4 seconds TOTAL from entry; no matched baseline body-ready measurement is supplied. Ordinary original-text/return preserves document, Find, loaded range and body scroll at the same settled 1440x900 viewport. Controls show retired scope, changed selection and unmount start no fallback GET or late body write; a failed fresh read stops visibly after that one attempt. Explicit refresh remains a new read. No write or native execution occurred, an unrelated POST outcome remains unconfirmed, and business adoption and native lineage are unknown. Decide whether two startup GETs invalidate the recovered reading and what performance conclusion is justified.
evals.expected_output: Accepts the supplied automatic current-report recovery and ordinary Reader return despite two startup GETs, while retaining the initial failure and total body-ready timing. Requires the bounded current-selection and full identity/proof guards, keeps failed recovery visible, and makes no unsupported speedup, authority, adoption or execution claim.
expectations: Accepts the supported recovered full-body and ordinary Reader-return result despite two startup GETs; does not require manual refresh or minimize requests at the expense of correct reading
Rejects adoption of absent, null or inconsistent initial proof and old preview text; accepts only the fresh current packet after complete existing identity and physical-source validation

Limits automatic recovery to one bounded fresh read while both current selection generation/scope and inventory takeover remain valid; preserves retirement, selection-change, unmount and late-write guards and stops visibly on fresh-read failure
Retains the first failure and 2.4-second total entry-to-full-body timing rather than restarting the clock at fallback; makes no speedup claim without a matched body-ready comparison

Preserves explicit refresh as a new read and does not promote reading evidence into write authority, business adoption, native execution or lineage; does not resend the unconfirmed POST or invent live interaction

evals.name: reader-find-loaded-window-and-history-return
evals.prompt: Audit only supplied synthetic observation records; no screenshots, live browser or write access is available. A retained Reader belongs to the verified resource session-example/current. Its initial newest window is a strict subset of the conversation, with earlier pages not loaded. Find is focused with query SYNTHETIC-ANCHOR and reports 0/0. The only explanation of search scope is inside a source-information disclosure that closes when Find receives focus. A proposed report says the whole conversation lost the question and recommends replacing Find with full-history global search. Later records for the same resource and Reader show the user opening History, loading the earlier question window, and finding SYNTHETIC-ANCHOR at 1/1 with the question's surrounding text. Query and resource identity remain unchanged; returning restores the same detail and wall selection. Both records use the same settled desktop viewport and reading container. A separate healthy control is an ordinary host without an optional scope declaration: it supplies complete loaded coverage of its declared conversation and Find 0/0 for an absent term. The supplied product acceptance contract for the repair makes scope information visible for a declaring host while Find is focused OR its query is nonempty, including a collapsed Find control. Clearing alone keeps focus, so the scope information remains visible; clearing and then blurring hides it. Pagination retains the query and recalculates against the loaded range; return retains the same resource, loaded range and work context. A host without that declaration retains its existing query, pagination, scroll and return behavior and receives no imposed hint or new clear/scroll semantics. These repair states are requirements, not supplied observations of a repaired render. Explain what the initial and later observations establish, identify the usability defect, and define minimal acceptance for the shared Reader repair. Include focused-empty Find, a nonempty query when Find collapses in a narrower desktop container, clearing versus leaving Find, pagination, and return. Mark unsupplied render states as unverified. Do not access production, preload all history, invent a new Reader or execution identity, or claim visual acceptance from these text records.
evals.expected_output: Rejects whole-conversation data loss from a partial-window 0/0 and accepts the later scoped hit and same-resource return as supplied observations. Identifies the unavailable scope explanation while Find is active, routes a minimal optional scope affordance to the shared Reader owner, and defines visible-state and reading-continuity checks while preserving ordinary hosts. Accepts the complete-coverage absent-term control and leaves actual pixels unverified.
expectations: Limits the initial 0/0 to the loaded newest window; does not infer whole-conversation absence or data loss and uses the existing History path to expand scope
Accepts the supplied later 1/1 and preserved same-resource return without recasting the original 0/0 as a Find matching-algorithm failure

Identifies the active Find scope explanation hidden by the disclosure as a usability defect; proposes making scope observable at the shared Reader owner without a replacement Reader, new identity or mandatory full-history preload

Requires scope information to remain visible for focused empty Find and a nonempty query when Find collapses in a narrower desktop container, with clear-and-blur behavior specified; does not substitute a changed viewport for a matched before/after comparison
Preserves query, loaded range, current resource/document and return context through pagination and reentry, and includes an ordinary host without the optional scope declaration as a healthy control
Accepts the separate complete-coverage absent-term 0/0 as a scoped no-match result, rather than treating every zero as broken or unknown
Separates supplied text observations and proposed acceptance from actual visual evidence; does not claim live screenshots, browser verification or write/execution authority

evals.name: current-pending-drift-does-not-compose-acceptance
evals.prompt: Judge acceptance from supplied synthetic records only; no live tools or screenshots are available. Required criterion A1 is frozen: from a currently confirmed waiting item in Needs Me, open that same question's original text and options, enter its surrounding conversation, then return to the same work context while remaining read-only. At T0, fresh list evidence confirms question Q pending for session-example/current, runtime R and witness W, but its detail read fails and the journey stops. At T1, a nonstructured follow-up message occurs. Fresh same-identity evidence now says Q unknown, with boundary 'whether the later message resolved it is unconfirmed' and can_answer=false; Q's original text and options remain readable. At T2, All view successfully opens Q's read-only original text and options, follows its native anchor, finds the text, and returns to the same detail and wall selection. Separate component tests pass a pending happy path and reject retired or wrong-identity callbacks. An author proposes combining those component tests with the T2 journey to mark A1 met, or treating Q's absence from Needs Me as a filter bug. Decide the supported acceptance state, what may be delivered now, and the next permissible observation. As a separate hypothetical healthy control, a naturally occurring fresh pending question with verified matching session/runtime/witness completes the entire A1 journey; explain how that control would be judged without pretending it happened in T0-T2. Do not answer or approve a real question, start a writer, manufacture a pending state or poll without a bound.
evals.expected_output: Preserves A1 as not met by T0-T2 while recognizing the delivered historical read-only journey and separate component evidence. Does not infer resolution, ongoing pending or a filter bug from the unknown question. Requires a naturally available fresh same-identity pending sample for the remaining formal journey, permits independent completed work to ship, and accepts the hypothetical complete pending control only within its stated scope.
expectations: Keeps the original current-pending A1 criterion unresolved because T0 stopped at the failed detail read; does not compose a component pending positive with the T2 historical journey into a single successful formal journey
Recognizes T2's original-text/options, anchor, Find and same-context return as valid supplied historical read-only evidence, rather than failing all delivered reading functionality
Keeps Q unknown after T1, neither resolved nor currently pending; does not renew attention from retained original text or assume Needs Me omitting that unknown item is a filter defect
Keeps the failed T0 detail observation and the later successful T2 read distinct; does not infer a unique transport root cause or permanent reliability from later success

Continues independently authorized completed delivery while retaining the missing criterion and its recovery condition: a naturally occurring fresh pending question bound to matching session/runtime/witness, then the complete Needs Me-to-context-and-return journey
Does not manufacture pending, answer or approve a question, start a new writer, expand authority or prescribe unbounded polling to obtain an acceptance sample

Accepts the separate hypothetical complete fresh-pending control as satisfying A1 for that control, while leaving the actual T0-T2 result unresolved and making no overall product or live visual-completion claim

evals.name: dashboard-copy-necessity-with-honest-state-controls
evals.prompt: Audit only these supplied render inventories for an agent workbench. Its user needs to find work requiring an answer, inspect the latest report, and open its original conversation. The user has rejected clutter and explanatory prose that does not help those tasks. Both inventories show the same tasks, native reading links and authoritative facts: 50 records loaded; total count unavailable; current execution state unavailable for some records; one worker-list refresh failed after a successful read at 09:14; a latest report lacks a timestamp; dispatch ownership and native upstream lineage are unavailable. These facts must remain accurate, not guessed as zero, idle, completed or absent work. Inventory A repeats the following product-authored text across its ordinary overview and detail: A1 '只计已确认执行；未读到状态不代表没有工作。'; A2 '读取超时，请刷新后继续。Worker 列表保留上次读取的记录，远端状态尚未确认。'; A3 '记录或状态未读全'; A4 '已载入 50 · 总数未确认'; A5 '读取范围 · 部分来源未读到'; A6 '只读来源采集的原生回报 · 回报不等于成果已采用或业务验收通过。'; A7 the heading '最近回报' followed by '时间未记录'; A8 '未保存有效派发声明'; A9 '未知：没有原生上下游证据'. Inventory B uses '已载入 50 条', a localized 'Worker 列表更新失败' with a Retry button and '上次更新 09:14', a short unavailable state beside affected objects, and a dash for the missing report time. A single optional '连接详情' opens the affected sources, partial coverage and raw diagnostic facts; unavailable dispatch or upstream fields are retained there rather than repeated in the ordinary report. It keeps the latest report body and original-conversation control visible. Additional supplied controls are C1 a destructive End task confirmation '结束任务将丢失未保存内容' where that loss is established; C2 active Reader Find showing '仅查找已载入记录' because older pages are not loaded, with the existing Load earlier control; C3 an unknown execution state with the original reading link still available; C4 the localized refresh failure, last-good time and Retry action in B; C5 the original Reader quoting A6 verbatim as an attributed historical message, not product-authored interface guidance. Give a disposition for A1-A9 and C1-C5, identifying what changes in the user's decision or action if text is removed, shortened or relocated. Compare A and B's task usability without inventing new observations, a live browser run, user adoption or an aesthetic score. Do not rewrite historical originals or remove truthful failure states merely to make the page cleaner.
evals.expected_output: Rejects A's repeated explanatory and defensive presentation against the stated task while preserving its necessary state facts. Prefers B's concise scoped count, localized recovery and optional diagnostics; handles each A item by its function rather than banning its words. Retains C1-C5, including the necessary Find scope and verbatim source quote, and leaves actual rendered geometry and daily adoption unverified.
expectations: Dispositions A1-A9 individually or in explicitly mapped groups; identifies repeated coverage explanation, producer self-defense, missing-field narration and internal dispatch/lineage language as presentation problems rather than automatically necessary because true
Preserves the failed-refresh fact, last-good time and actionable retry from A2 or B; shortening or relocation does not turn failure into current success or silently present retained data as fresh

Accepts B's loaded-count scope without inventing a total, and preserves unavailable execution and coverage facts through concise local state plus reachable details; does not replace unknown with zero, idle, complete or no work

Keeps C1's established destructive consequence at the action and C2's loaded-window scope observable while Find is active, with the existing earlier-page reading path; does not remove necessary warnings under a general less-text rule
Keeps C3's honest unknown and useful reading path, and C4's localized failure/retry; treats the necessary fact separately from redundant wording and placement
Recognizes C5 as attributed source content, preserves its verbatim wording and original-reading behavior, and does not flag or rewrite it as product-authored explanatory copy

Uses the reader's task and concrete information loss to compare A and B; does not certify quality from fewer words, a keyword blacklist, an arbitrary word budget, passing geometry, an invented interaction or a generic aesthetic score
